q: The resource theory of thermodynamics in one-shot quantum information uses 'thermal operations' (interactions with a heat bath at temperature T). The second law in this framework says a state ρ can be converted to σ by thermal operations iff:
opts: The free energies satisfy F(ρ) ≥ F(σ): F = Tr[Hρ] − TS(ρ)
The Rényi divergences D_α(ρ||γ) ≥ D_α(σ||γ) for all α ≥ 0 (where γ is the Gibbs state)
ρ and σ commute with H
exp: In the one-shot resource theory (Brandão-Horodecki-Oppenheim-Streltsov-Wehner 2015): ρ → σ by thermal operations iff D_α(ρ||γ) ≥ D_α(σ||γ) for all α ≥ 0 (the 'thermomajorization' condition in terms of Rényi divergences). This is an infinite family of constraints — the single free energy F(ρ) ≥ F(σ) is only the first-order (i.i.d.) condition.
